wave: VERIFICATION BLINDNESS -- runtime::systemize computes 8 independent coding_admission.blockers conditions (REPO_GATE_NOT_READY, DOCS_GATE_NOT_READY, ADL_DIAGNOSTICS_PRESENT, ADL_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATED, INVENTORY_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED, CENSUS_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED, NORMALIZATION_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED, SEMANTIC_EXTRACTION_ACCOUNTING_NOT_CLOSED, DEPENDENCY_CLOSURE_NOT_CLOSED) and had zero direct unit test coverage anywhere in the runtime crate. The sole indirect test (in apps/cli) only asserted that CLI exit was an error, never which blockers fired.
wave_title: Nineteenth generation this cycle. Continuing the verification-blindness angle opened in generation 18 (parse_repo_manifest), this generation audits runtime::systemize, the central report-building function invoked by every `atlas systemize` run.
priority_classification: verification blindness -- not a live production bug (systemize's 8 blocker conditions are, as far as this generation independently confirmed, currently computed correctly), but a real gap in this project's own verification coverage: a plausible future regression (e.g. two blocker string literals swapped between adjacent if-blocks) would leave every existing test green.
gap_discovered_by: Self-directed review of runtime/src/lib.rs (lines 160-284, systemize()) after grepping the whole workspace for `systemize(` and finding exactly one call site under test, in apps/cli/src/main.rs's a_repository_with_no_admitted_manifest_makes_systemize_exit_non_zero.
key_finding: The only test touching systemize() asserted solely `assert_eq!(err, "CODING_ADMISSION_NOT_ALLOWED")` -- the CLI's own generic error code for admission refusal, identical regardless of which of the 8 independent blocker conditions actually fired, or how many. It never read back the `--out` report file, so it could not distinguish correct blocker computation from a swapped label, a wrongly-suppressed condition, or a wrongly-raised one. Since a bare git repository with no `.atlas/` directory at all guarantees at least one blocker fires (trivially, by construction of the test fixture), the assertion was satisfied by construction and exercised none of systemize's actual per-condition logic.
verification_before_acting: Read runtime::systemize's full implementation (runtime/src/lib.rs:160-284) directly, confirming it computes each of the 8 blocker conditions independently and appends matching string-literal labels to a Vec in a fixed, hardcoded order.
Grepped the whole workspace for `systemize(` to confirm the apps/cli test is genuinely the only test exercising it end-to-end, and confirmed no direct unit test exists in the runtime crate itself.

Ran a real CLI reproduction against an actual bare git repository (no .atlas/repo.toml, no docs) to observe the REAL, current blockers list before hardcoding any assertion, rather than guessing or trusting a description: confirmed ["REPO_GATE_NOT_READY", "DOCS_GATE_NOT_READY"] is what a bare repo fixture actually produces today.

design_decisions.question: Fix production code, or strengthen the test?
design_decisions.decision: Strengthen the test only. Direct reading of systemize's implementation confirmed the 8 blocker conditions are currently computed and labeled correctly; the gap is that no test would catch a regression in that logic, not that the logic is wrong today.

design_decisions.question: How to falsify a test-strengthening change with no live production bug to revert-and-confirm against?
design_decisions.decision: Inverted falsification: backed up runtime/src/lib.rs, injected the exact plausible bug described (swapped the "DOCS_GATE_NOT_READY" and "ADL_DIAGNOSTICS_PRESENT" string literals between their two adjacent if-blocks), re-ran the strengthened test and confirmed it failed with the exact expected mismatch, then restored the file from backup and confirmed git diff --stat showed zero residual change.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: The strengthened test now reads back the systemize report's coding_admission.blockers array and asserts its exact contents for a real, minimal bare-repository fixture, closing a verification gap where the prior assertion (a generic CLI error code) could not distinguish correct per-condition blocker computation from a swapped, suppressed, or spuriously-raised condition.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added a serde_json read-back of the --out report file plus an exact-match assertion on coding_admission.blockers to apps/cli/src/main.rs's a_repository_with_no_admitted_manifest_makes_systemize_exit_non_zero. Falsified by temporarily swapping the DOCS_GATE_NOT_READY/ADL_DIAGNOSTICS_PRESENT string literals in runtime::systemize's real implementation, confirming the strengthened test failed with the exact expected mismatch (left: [...ADL_DIAGNOSTICS_PRESENT...], right: [...DOCS_GATE_NOT_READY...]), directly proving the old bare error-code assertion would not have caught this class of bug, then restoring the file from a byte-for-byte backup and confirming git diff --stat produced no output.
